headline: Approves $132,000 HarborWalk grant and 1.03 commercial tax shift; rejects tax parity and withdraws RC40 lot-size change.
summary: Council heard an update on the wastewater plant upgrade at Essex Ave., with construction planned through 2030. It approved a $132,000 state grant for HarborWalk signs and wayfinding. It set the fiscal 2027 tax shift at 1.03, rejecting a tax rate with no shift, and approved removing a newspaper publication step for fee changes.
decisions: Approved appointing Angela Sanfilippo to the Fisheries Commission, term to end 2/15/2029, 9-0.
Approved the consent agenda as amended, 9-0.
Referred the matter to Planning and Development and the Planning Board, and set a public hearing for December 8, 2026 with notice to abutters waived, 9-0.
Approved accepting a $132,000 Massachusetts Downtown Initiative Capital Grant for HarborWalk and wayfinding work, 8 to 1.
Approved accepting a framed portrait of former city clerk Joanne Senos, with an estimated value of $150, as a gift, 8 to 0 with 1 recused.
Withdrew, without prejudice, the proposal to raise the minimum lot area in the RC40 Coastal Residential district from 20,000 to 40,000 square feet, 9-0.
Failed, 2 in favor and 7 opposed, a motion to set a tax factor of 1 so that all property classes pay the same rate.
Approved a residential tax factor of 0.9973 for fiscal 2027, which sets the commercial, industrial, and personal property shift at 1.03, 8 to 0 with 1 opposed.
Approved removing the requirement to publish fee changes in a local newspaper; the fee schedule must still be posted on the city website, 8 to 0 with 1 absent.
discussion: Members asked about the timeline, cost controls, pile design, and grant funding for the Essex Ave. wastewater plant upgrade.

Concerns were raised about the HarborWalk grant, including signs and thermoplastic markers on the working waterfront, possible effects on trucks and boats, and the lack of public input before the grant was applied for.
Business owners asked the council to keep the 1.03 commercial tax shift, and a resident asked for 1.05. Members debated a flat tax factor of 1 for all property classes.
A member asked for stricter speed limit enforcement after recent accidents. Another asked whether the council could put forward ordinances on e-bikes.
